request.state:
Target: Microsoft (MSFT). Microsoft develops software and cloud services including Windows, Microsoft 365 and Azure, and operates gaming, business-software and related technology businesses.

Focal announcement: Microsoft Build 2025: The age of AI agents and building the open agentic web.

Decision cutoff: 2025-05-19T23:59:59-04:00. Only information available before this cutoff is admissible.

Source: Microsoft Build 2025: The age of AI agents and building the open agentic web. Published: 2025-05-19. URL: https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2025/05/19/microsoft-build-2025-the-age-of-ai-agents-and-building-the-open-agentic-web.

Condensed source facts; other details are omitted: Hear the news as an AI-generated audio overview made using Microsoft 365 Copilot. For example, 15 million developers are already using GitHub Copilot, and features like agent mode and code review are streamlining the way they code, check, deploy and troubleshoot. Hundreds of thousands of customers are using Microsoft 365 Copilot to help research, brainstorm and develop solutions, and more than 230,000 organizations — including 90% of the Fortune 500 — have already used Copilot Studio to build AI agents and automations. As the home of over 150 million developers, this reinforces our commitment to open, collaborative, AI-powered software development. With the general availability of Azure AI Foundry Agent Service, Microsoft is bringing new capabilities to empower professional developers to orchestrate multiple specialized agents to handle complex tasks, including bringing Semantic Kernel and AutoGen into a single, developer-focused SDK and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) support.

The exact historical text version is unverified. This is an incomplete source-based reconstruction.

Expectations: No point-in-time analyst consensus or market-implied expectation is available.

No company-wide comparable financial baselines or incremental magnitude inputs were supplied. Do not infer that a large headline amount is material to the target.

The broad market (SPY) showed a substantial past rise over the recent trading week, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The broad market (SPY) showed a strong past rise over the recent trading month, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The broad market (SPY)'s recent daily variability was moderate. Variability describes the size of ordinary fluctuations, not their future direction.

Over the recent trading week, the stock showed very small outperformance relative to the broad market.

Over the recent trading month, the stock showed substantial outperformance relative to the broad market.

These are coarse descriptions computed from observed historical inputs. Strong past movement or relative strength is not evidence that the next return must continue or reverse.

The previously fitted market-only reference model favored an upward return beyond the neutral band. Its leading outcome was only slightly favored. It still assigned meaningful possibility to a return inside the narrow neutral band and a downward return beyond the neutral band. This is a training-only model forecast, not an observed outcome or independent news evidence.

The neutral return band's half-width is much narrower than the code-computed ordinary five-session variability scale. An irrelevant article does not eliminate ordinary price movement; this is not a calculated class probability.

Forecast target: entry is the first regular-session open after the cutoff; exit is the fifth session close, counting entry as session one. Raw return above +1% is up; within inclusive -1% to +1% is flat; below -1% is down. The initial pre-entry reaction is outside this target.

Do not invent analyst consensus, incremental target sales, new corporate cash payments, or an already-priced news reaction.
